page: Google Cloud Platform n4d-highmem-4 is an x86_64 architecture server powered by a dedicated AMD EPYC 9B45 processor. It features 4 vCPUs mapped to 2 physical cores with multithreading enabled. The instance is configured with 32 GB of system memory, yielding a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8 GB per core. It does not include local storage or integrated GPUs, and has zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Performance benchmarks indicate strong single-core capabilities alongside moderate multi-core scaling. The single-core stress-ng CPU performance and single-threaded gzip compression and bzip3 decompression benchmarks rank in the top tier, placing in the top 10% of tested systems. Conversely, multi-threaded bzip3 decompression falls into the bottom 25%, highlighting a performance tradeoff when scaling parallel decompression tasks. Memory bandwidth and database operations, including Redis SET operations at 7.4 million operations per second, consistently register in the average range.

Given its high memory density relative to compute resources, the n4d-highmem-4 offers qualitative cost efficiency for memory-bound workloads that do not require massive parallel processing. It is well-suited for medium-scale database operations, caching layers, and memory-intensive web serving. However, its poor performance in medium-sized LLM inference tasks makes it unsuitable for modern AI generation workloads.
